_note: Rule 3 (delete-outside-disposable) fixtures, CONTRACT.md #6 table (B) -- min 10, including block-outside, allow-per-location, `..` escape, comma-joined -LiteralPath, lower-case remove-item, pm-delete-allow consume-on-use (before/after), and subagent denial. Cases whose command references a dynamically-sandboxed path use the '{{BAD_PATH}}' placeholder -- test_tool_discipline.py substitutes it with a concrete absolute path under the per-test sandbox before invoking the guard (and into pm_allow_seed entries identically, so the two sides compare equal after normalisation).

M-9b/F-18: '..' resolves against the HOOK PROCESS cwd, not payload.cwd. test_tool_discipline.py os.chdir()s into a fresh temp dir before invoking the guard directly (needs_chdir), then restores cwd in finally. dist/../../ escapes above the chdir base, landing outside every allowed substring.
2026-08-29 fix: a comma-joined -LiteralPath list used to be one token, so one allowed path let the whole list through. Every entry must be independently allowed.
text-kind case-insensitivity: lower-case 'remove-item' must be caught exactly like 'Remove-Item'.

round-3 fix: uses parity.py's REAL setup schema ({kind:'pm_delete_allow', paths:[...]}) instead of the {{BAD_PATH}}/dynamic convention invented in round-1, which parity.py never understood -- the literal '{{BAD_PATH}}' text has no '/' or '.', so it was never even recognised as a path token, Rule 3 never engaged, and both sides trivially agreed on ALLOW for the wrong reason (both unprepared, not both correct). The target here is a RELATIVE path with no '..' segment, so it is compared as-is (never dotdot-resolved) but IS resolved via _full_path()/process cwd for the pm-delete-allow comparison specifically -- and since neither run_old_side() nor run_new_side() pass an explicit subprocess cwd=, BOTH sides inherit parity.py's own process cwd identically, so a plain relative string needs no sandbox-path templating to line up on both sides of the allow-file/command comparison. Main chain (no agent_id/transcript) + the exact relative path pre-authorised -> GRANT, exit 0. The full BEFORE/AFTER file-state proof of consume-on-use (granted once, then blocked on an identical second run against the SAME state) cannot be expressed as one parity fixture -- parity.py reseeds fresh per side and per case, it never chains two runs -- so that proof lives in test_tool_discipline.py's check_consume_on_use_before_after(), which calls the guard directly, twice, against one sandbox it fully controls.

round-3 fix: id kept for traceability, scope corrected. The original 'run again after r3-14 consumed it' framing does not fit parity.py's per-case fresh-sandbox model (see r3-14's note); reinterpreted as the branch it can actually test honestly: pm-delete-allow EXISTS (unlike r3-01, which has no allow file at all) but lists only an UNRELATED path, so the target is not covered -> still BLOCKED. This exercises 'entry present, target not listed' as its own real, seeded branch, distinct from both r3-01 (no file) and r3-14 (exact match). The genuine before/after consume-on-use proof lives in test_tool_discipline.py's check_consume_on_use_before_after().

PM allowlist is main-chain only (I-6). round-3 fix: real setup (see r3-14's note on why a plain relative path needs no sandbox templating) -- the allow file genuinely lists the EXACT target path this time, so the block is provably caused by the non-empty agent_id (subagent), not by an unseeded/absent allowlist.

PE-1: agent_id empty AND transcript_path under /subagents/, path pre-authorised. OLD (agent_id-only check) treats this as main chain and GRANTS (consumes). NEW (two-signal is_main_chain) also checks the transcript path and BLOCKS. Deliberate tightening, never a loosening. round-3 fix: real setup (r3-14's note) so the allow file genuinely lists the target -- the block is provably caused by the two-signal check, not by an unseeded allowlist. transcript_path uses ${SUB_TRANSCRIPT} (parity.py's resolved placeholder, a path containing '/subagents/'); is_main_chain only regex-matches this string, it never touches the filesystem, so the placeholder need not point at a real file.
